title: Appeal of RE Mark Chavalas vs. Northern Illinois Presbytery
disposition_detail: The SJC found the appeal judicially out of order and dismissed it under SJC Manual 11.6, while suspending Presbytery’s judgment under BCO 42-7. It treated Chavalas’s resignation as neither abandonment nor grounds for a rebuke.
first_summary: Chavalas appealed a Northern Illinois Presbytery judgment, but testimony cited by both parties was missing from the record. Because recording-machine failures made the required transcripts unavailable and Presbytery could not cure the defect, the SJC found the appeal judicially out of order, dismissed it under SJC Manual 11.6, and suspended Presbytery’s judgment under BCO 42-7.
summary: Chavalas appealed a Northern Illinois Presbytery judgment, but testimony cited by both parties was missing from the record. Because recording-machine failures made the required transcripts unavailable and Presbytery could not cure the defect, the SJC found the appeal judicially out of order, dismissed it under SJC Manual 11.6, and suspended Presbytery’s judgment under BCO 42-7. Chavalas’s later resignation did not abandon the appeal because he had appealed beforehand after a regular trial; no rebuke was issued.

sources.supports: Case identity, adopted disposition, reasoning, suspension of judgment, resignation qualification, absence of rebuke, vote, and approval.

evidence_notes.identity_and_adoption: The case heading identifies Case 2003-1 and the parties; the recommendation was adopted and approved by the full SJC on March 4, 2004 (printed pp. 105–106, lines 13–17, 40–52).
evidence_notes.dispute: The appeal record lacked transcripts of lower-court testimony cited by both parties (printed p. 105, lines 19–30).
evidence_notes.outcomes_and_reasons: The SJC found the case judicially out of order, dismissed it under Manual 11.6, and suspended Presbytery’s judgment under BCO 42-7 because the missing transcripts could not be supplied after recording-machine failures (printed p. 105, lines 17–30, 34–38).
evidence_notes.qualifications: The resignation did not abandon the earlier appeal following a regular trial, and no rebuke was necessary because Presbytery had an opportunity to cure the record but could not do so (printed p. 105, lines 32–38).
evidence_notes.incorporated_decisions: No decision was incorporated by reference; the cited BCO and Manual provisions supplied procedural authority (printed p. 105, lines 17–25, 34–38).

source_limits: The source does not describe the substance of Presbytery’s judgment or the underlying charges, so the synopsis is limited to the record defect and procedural relief.
